speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to ensure your safety, have you had any fainting, confusion, or difficulty breathing? REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG) and Complete Blood Count (CBC). REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the normal ECG, CBC, and metabolic panel help rule out acute cardiac ischemia and severe electrolyte imbalances. To clarify your condition, have the vomiting and chest pain been present since the onset of your illness, and is the pain sharp or burning in nature? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture).

The combination of forceful vomiting following alcohol consumption, a subsequent choking episode, and chest pain in a middle-aged male is highly suggestive of esophageal rupture. The inability to communicate effectively indicates severe distress or aspiration. While the initial workup ruled out cardiac causes, the clinical picture strongly points to an esophageal tear rather than simple gastroesophageal reflux or viral gastritis.
